summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC Ishaq old houses/34)

data.turoyo: Ánnaqqa mədčimənto ḥaṯto w maʕmár!
data.translation: Now take new cement and build!

rationale: New Imperativ box, singular command in an independent building-material clause.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 84/92)

data.turoyo: ʕAmerulli ǧeməʕ dlo šəbebək w kalešu gawe w sumulle tarʕo, d lo ʕobər fərṭaʕno taḥt u tarʕo,
data.translation: baut mir eine Moschee ohne Fenster, kalkt sie inwendig und macht ihre Türe so, dass kein Floh unter ihr hinein kann;

rationale: New Imperativ box, reduced plural command with beneficiary; no base form is inferred from the reduction.

summary: New box Nomen Actionis: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (MAC Ishaq Material culture/27)

data.turoyo: Ḥatta, komar, maʕmárralle i+dayro, yani mʕawanne bi+ʕmara di+dayro támoste, Mōr Malke.
data.translation: They even, it says, built the monastery for him, like, they helped with the building of the monastery there too, Mor Malke.

rationale: New Nomen Actionis box: definite nominal building task governed by bi- and with a di- complement; not evidence for an Infinitiv.

summary: New box Nomen Actionis: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (94/18)

data.turoyo: An naḥote ste konəḥtənne w kosaymi ḥaǧat l ʕmara mənne.
data.translation: Diese behauen sie und machen daraus Baumaterial.

rationale: Nomen Actionis with l- purpose: building material. The edition translation is retained.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (61/299)

data.turoyo: W lə kmətyaqnat stine, kal komaʕmalle arbʕo qusre me qarʕe da ənsanat l ḥeḏər i walaye.”
data.translation: Und wenn du es nicht glauben willst: Da, vier Schlösser hat er aus den Menschen schädeln um die Stadt herum gebaut."

rationale: New ko-Preterit box: ko- plus Preterit agent suffix, presenting visible completed building.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC NE Mem and Zin/27)

data.turoyo: Kalé bayne falge+du+baḥar ʕamiro u+quṣrayḏux.
data.translation: Here’s your castle built within the sea’s midst.

rationale: Thin inherited Part cell: masculine result-state predicate beside inherited feminine forms.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (PrS 86/19)

data.turoyo: Kətli məḏ̣ḏ̣ara ʕal ḥa qayso ʕamərto, l nošo lo maʕamrole, li arʕo maʕamrola, knofəq biya ʕaskar — u šəblo.
data.translation: Ich weiss ein Zimmerchen, gebaut auf ein Holz; kein Mensch hat es gebaut, sondern die Erde hat es gebaut, es entstehen in ihm Soldaten. (Die Aehre).

rationale: Thin Part cell: the full ear-of-grain riddle makes the nonhuman building metaphor intelligible.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (68/35)

data.turoyo: Maṯe kəḏʕina, d kətyo i ʕitaṯe d bu doro da tloṯo ʕamərto.
data.translation: Daher wissen wir, daß unsere Kirche im Laufe des dritten Jahrhunderts erbaut ist.

rationale: Fifth Part example contrasts ʕamərto with dated finite ʕamiro forms at 68/28–31.

summary: New sense 2: (fig.) eine Angelegenheit in Ordnung bringen, regeln

data.gloss: (fig.) eine Angelegenheit in Ordnung bringen, regeln

rationale: 97/4 has the vizier as agent and the king's lack of a wife as the matter under discussion; no building or material patient occurs. One clear contextual attestation, with homonym assignment still an editorial question; no marriage-specific sense is created.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/24)

data.turoyo: Qām maʕmárralle dayro bi+qriṯo.
data.translation: They up and built a monastery for him in the village.

rationale: Standalone building clause with overt monastery and beneficiary; fills the four-example Preterit cell to five.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Interview 2/247)

data.turoyo: elo ann+avayani, dawla d ăḷo driše du+ʕamo, lu+ʕamo maʕmáḷḷelanne, ŭ hawxa.
data.translation: but the buildings, thanks to the people, the people built them for us, and so forth.

rationale: Unusual suffix chain with topicalized buildings, l-marked agent and first-person plural beneficiary; retained beyond the routine cell target for argument coding.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC YT LIFE STORY/74)

data.turoyo: Aṯən, maʕmárranne bote ḥaṯe, ŭ mḥaṯḥaṯṯe ab+botaṯṯe.
data.translation: They came back, they built themselves new houses, and they renovated their houses.

rationale: Unusual -anne form contrasts new construction with renovation in one independent sentence; segmentation remains a question.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (57/148)

data.turoyo: Kḥozeno aq qarʕe, d qṭilux w maʕmallux appe.
data.translation: Ich sehe ja die Köpfe, die du abgeschlagen und mit denen du gebaut hast.

rationale: Unusual second-person Preterit with r/l assimilation and overt material reference.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.5/1)

data.turoyo: u rabano di qriṯo haka di walaye məftakalle omər an naʕimani kulle falite bas saḥat w baz zabiqone, gəmaʕmannolən madrase, w mitaltəmi maš šuqone,
data.translation: Der Herrscher des Dorfes oder der Stadt dachte sich: All diese Kinder laufen frei auf den Plätzen und in den Straßen herum, ich werde für sie eine Schule bauen, damit sie von den Straßen geholt werden

rationale: Fifth Infectum example: explicit school, plural beneficiary and contracted first-person form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (LuF 3/34)

data.turoyo: Annaqla gaban feme dag gube, komaʕamri kefe ḥeḏər feme du gubo.
data.translation: Nun pflegt man bei uns um den Rand der Zisternen herum Steine aufzuschichten.

rationale: Distinct materials-object frame already covered by inherited 'pile up'; concrete masonry context beyond routine building.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (97/4)

data.turoyo: Ḥa yawmo karəx u məǧləs diḏe, du malkano, omər: “Ya u malkayḏan, dlo ḥurma lo koweluxyo.” — “E”, — omər, — “kale u wazirayḏi, aṣl hiye yo. D hiye maʕmər, aṣl hiye yo w širatkar diḏi.”
data.translation: Eines Tages trat die Ratsversammlung des Königszusammen und sprach: Unser König! du darfst nicht ohne Frau bleiben. - Eh, sprach er, da ist mein Wesir, auf den kommt es an. Er mag das in Ordnung bringen; auf ihn kommt es an, der ist mein Berater. -

rationale: Only attestation of new figurative sense 2; the full exchange supplies the affair that the vizier is to arrange.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (113/176)

data.turoyo: I arʕo maḥərwalla, maʕəmralla? Aməlli, be mə saymono!
data.translation: soll ich die Weit verwüsten oder aufbauen? Sage mir, was ich tun soll!

rationale: Unusual contracted -alla in parallel verbs, preserving the edition's Weit and leaving suffix segmentation open.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Ishaq Material culture/19)

data.turoyo: Dəmmina am+maʕəmronayḏa mánwayne?
data.translation: Let’s say who were its builders?

rationale: Thin III Part act. cell: possessive builder noun, with the place recoverable from the reference.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (94/4)

data.turoyo: Kito qəsm mu ʕamo, qaṭoʕe di šeno w maʕəmrone dab bote ne.
data.translation: Ein Teil der Leute besteht aus Steinhauern und Maurern, die Häuser bauen.

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: builders with overt genitive building product.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (94/20)

data.turoyo: U šuġlo du maʕəmrono ste: kmaʕmər.
data.translation: Die Arbeit des Maurers ist das Bauen.

rationale: Thin Part act. cell: builder noun beside its finite building verb in a self-contained occupational definition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/26)

data.turoyo: Dínaqqa dʔoṯənwa a+mšiḥoye, yani, dínaqqa dmaqəbliwa i+haymonuṯo də Mšiḥo, direk maʕəmriwa ʕito bi+qriṯayo.
data.translation: When the Christians would come, like, when they embraced the faith of Christ, they would immediately build a church in that village.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: real discourse replaces reliance on two bare inherited paradigm examples.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/86)

data.turoyo: Ŭ hawxa maʕəmriwa ab+bote, ŭ howanwa qawye ġắlabe,
data.translation: And like so, they would build the houses, and they were very strong,

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: plural building product and customary construction, with a literal aligned cut.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/87)

data.turoyo: Kə́twaylan, dəmmina, hostawat di+qriṯo, əzzanwa larwal, maʕəmriwa baq+qərya<woṯo> daṭ+ṭaye, dač+čəlkoye, larwal əzzanwa.
data.translation: We had, let’s say, village craftsmen, they would go out, they would build in the villages of Muslims, Yezidis, they would go out.

rationale: Fifth Infectum-wa example: building used absolutely with a village location.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Lahdo martyrdom/1)

data.turoyo: I ʕitaṯe yaʕni kṯuwe u hnayḏa alfo w ḥamməšmo əšne. Hən kəmmi noqəṣ ʕəsri, tleṯi yo hama kṯiwalle alfo w ḥamməšmo əšno d ʕamiro. ʕAtəqto yo.
data.translation: This church is dated to be 1500-year old. Some say it was built 20 or 30 years later but it is documented that it was built 1500 years ago. It is old.

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive cell: explicitly dated church construction without a builder.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/67)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr baš+šeṯ ŭ ʕəsri daʕiri, naqqa+ḥreto dʕamiro, hul la+tmone+ŭ+ʕəsri.
data.translation: After ’26, they returned, so it got built up again, until ’28.

rationale: Thin cell: settlement rebuilt after return, contrasting active III without adding a rebuilding sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (68/30)

data.turoyo: Kosomno zan, d i ʕito w u sur d Dyarbakər ʕam ḥḏoḏe ʕamiri.
data.translation: Ich vermute, daß die Kirche und die Mauer von Diyarbekir zur gleichen Zeit erbaut worden sind.

rationale: Thin cell: plural theme and simultaneous church/wall construction; conjecture is retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (68/31)

data.turoyo: M iḏe d bu tarix d Lubnan kəmqayəd komər: aʕ ʕitoṯe, d kətne b Mazopotamiya, d kətne b Beṯ Nahrin, kulle mu ṭaraf d Helane i malkṯo ʕamiri.
data.translation: Denn in der Geschichte des Libanon gibt der Verfasser an, daß die Kirchen in Mesopotamien, im Zweistromland, alle von der Königin Helene erbaut worden seien.

rationale: Fifth I Preterit Intransitive example: explicit mu ṭaraf d- agent with the patient-oriented I construction.

summary: Move tamo from the translation field to the end of the Turoyo quotation
before: tamo ‘I will go and build a village there for me and for my cousins’
after: I will go and build a village there for me and for my cousins

data.turoyo: gəd-əzzino maʕmárno-li qriṯo, eli w-l-ap=pismam-ayḏi tamo

rationale: The raw quotation places tamo before the opening translation quote. The supplied verse 36/146 likewise has ... lap pəsmamayḏi tamo. It is the Turoyo adverb translated as “there”, not part of the English translation.

summary: I contrasts finite patient-oriented ʕamiro/ʕamiri in dated building events with ʕamərto and masculine ʕamiro in result-state predicates. The inherited Part label is kept in the human layout; new box labels use Part act. as an alias, without creating a second cell or inferring Detransitive morphology.
68/31 has mu ṭaraf d Helane as agent with I ʕamiri; 68/32 presents the same builder as l Helane with active III. A German or English passive translation alone does not select a Detransitive box.

III Preterit allows l-marked agents, internal product suffixes and additional beneficiary suffixes. MAC NE Interview 2/247 and MAC YT LIFE STORY/59,74 show complex -anne/-ḷḷe-lan-ne forms; the readings are retained without a complete segmentation.
Infectum-wa appears in customary building accounts and under inability (MAC Ishaq Material culture/88–89); habitual meaning alone cannot characterize the box.

ʕmara occurs as a building task (MAC Ishaq Material culture/27; 94/18) and a concrete construction with layout/height (43,54,58). These are nominal evidence; an Infinitiv paradigm is not established. III association follows the neighboring active verb and remains provisional.

Existing 57/135,136 and 68/28,29 references already cover paired verses; repeated source occurrences do not require new examples. Several supplied no-add records have no verse; their analyses are explicitly unverified.
Should the building/flourishing homonyms be cross-referenced, especially the inherited ʕamər bayto idiom and MAC NE Interview 2/175? Is 97/4 best housed under ʕmr 2 III?
Confirm ʕmara as Nomen Actionis and its stem association; do layout/building uses merit separate nominal treatment rather than verb senses?

Collate 1/8: supplied maʕmər versus inherited mmaʕmər, and the inherited 'MUST BE 2ND STEM!' comment attached to the other Detransitive example. No stem move can be justified from the present source alone.
Parse -anne in MAC YT LIFE STORY/59,74, -ḷḷe-lan-ne at MAC NE Interview 2/247, and -alla at 113/176. Does kmaʕmarle at MAC YT LIFE STORY/74 belong to Infectum or ko-Preterit?
PrS 47/71 has final -le where the German has ihr. Confirm beneficiary segmentation; retain both texts without normalizing the suffix.
Please specify the inherited I 'Part' category and the source (+det) annotation at 57/138; neither supports silently relocating examples.
Built patient ranges from house and monastery to town/plain/world; kefe can name material assembled into masonry. These participant changes remain within the inherited building/piling gloss.
An egg and an ear of grain are described as built chambers in riddles; descriptive imagery does not establish a separate lexical sense.
